heloc.title: Pay a 2% HELOC closing charge outside the borrowed balance
heloc.inputs: $50,000 borrowed; constant 8%; ten-year draw then twenty-year repayment; 2% closing cost paid upfront; no annual fee.
steps: Keep the $50,000 contractual principal and gross disbursement; separately pay $1,000.
Read $49,000 as net initial cash; this matches a $1,000 deduction economically but not as gross disbursed cash.

expected.label: Net initial proceeds after closing costs

heloc.title: Start HELOC repayment without a draw period
heloc.inputs: $50,000 balance; constant 8%; zero years draw; twenty-year repayment; no closing cost; $120 annual fee entered.
steps: A zero-year draw produces no draw-period payment rows.
Annual fees apply only during draw in this model, so none is charged here.
Amortize $50,000 over 240 equal monthly payments beginning in month one.
heloc.answer: Monthly repayment: $418.22; modeled annual draw fees: $0.

heloc.title: Clamp an assumed HELOC borrowing ceiling at zero
heloc.inputs: $500,000 home value; $450,000 mortgage; hypothetical 80% maximum combined LTV.
steps: Subtract the entered $450,000 mortgage to get negative $50,000 headroom.
Clamp additional available credit to zero; this is not a negative loan, automatic approval or a payment quote.

home-equity-loan.title: Deduct $1,500 home equity closing costs from proceeds
home-equity-loan.inputs: $60,000 loan; 8% nominal rate; fifteen years; $1,500 closing costs deducted from proceeds.
steps: Repay $60,000 while receiving $58,500 after the deduction.
The monthly installment matches the separately-paid-cost example because the contractual principal is unchanged.
Use net initial cash once for the cash-flow APR and total-cost comparison.

home-equity-loan.title: Keep an upfront fee when the stated interest rate is zero
home-equity-loan.inputs: $60,000 loan; 0% stated rate; fifteen years; $1,500 closing costs paid upfront.
steps: Net initial cash is $60,000 minus the separate $1,500 charge.
The $1,500 cash-flow cost produces a positive modeled APR even though scheduled interest is zero.

debt-consolidation.title: Consolidate two different-rate cards with a five-year loan
debt-consolidation.inputs: Card A $5,000 at 22%, $150 fixed minimum; Card B $3,000 at 18%, $100 fixed minimum. New 10% loan, five years, 3% financed origination fee.
steps: Keep the current $250 monthly budget and roll freed payments to the highest-rate debt.
Compare the new contractual installment and interest plus the fee with that current plan; this is not an equal-budget comparison.
